qbox.target: Generator, no input group; tx/ty/tz move the box centre, sizex/sizey/sizez set extent.
qbox.notes: divisions takes any integer and stays all-quad. bevel_crease_mode is a toggle, not a menu.

extrude_faces.target: group is a primitive group; accepts an upstream group name or an inline list like "0 3-5".
extrude_faces.notes: Output identical to modeler::extrude (same P hash). Division parm is divs here, divisions on the modeler node.

insert_loop.target: group is an edge group; give ONE edge the new loop should cross, as "p<a>-<b>" or an upstream edge group name.
insert_loop.notes: mode 0 ignores dist/ratio; modes 1 and 2 insert two loops at once. For a single loop at an arbitrary ratio use polysplit edgepercent.

connect.target: grouptype token edge|point|primitive. Edge mode: list the ring edges to cut across (inline or group name). Point mode: two points on one face.
connect.notes: Edge-ring mode stays all-quad. Non-adjacent points or edges give a silent no-op or n-gons, so re-read the prim count.

bridge.target: srcgroup/dstgroup are edge groups naming the two boundary loops; inline "p<a>-<b>" lists work.
bridge.notes: Output identical to modeler::bridge (same counts). Output group toggles default to off on the native node.

fill_hole.target: group is the edge group of the hole boundary; inline "p<a>-<b>" list or an upstream edge group name.
fill_hole.notes: fillmode tokens none|tris|trifan|quadfan|quads|gridquads. modeler::fill_quads cannot do this, it silently ignores edge and point groups.

requad_ngon.target: group is a PRIMITIVE group of the faces to be replaced by a quad patch; boundary point count must be a multiple of 4.
requad_ngon.notes: mode tokens "5" grid, "4" quads, "3" fan. Edge or point grouptype is a silent no-op.

bevel_edges.target: group is an edge group (inline "p<a>-<b>" or a name); empty group plus ignoreflatedges=1 means only sharp edges get beveled.
bevel_edges.notes: filletshape tokens none|solid|crease|chamfer|round. Output identical to modeler::bevel (same P hash), and the native node has fewer parms.

shell.target: group is a primitive group; empty means all faces. Default value is the string "!_3d_hidden_primitives".
shell.notes: Same P hash as the native recipe. Use the native node when you need extrudeBack and extrudeSide as separate groups.

slide_edges.target: group is the edge loop to slide, inline "p<a>-<b>" list or an upstream edge group name.
slide_edges.notes: No native parametric equivalent. Even at slide=0 the P array changes, so never use it as an identity node.

edge_flow.target: group must be a real edge group, typically the loop written by polybevel offsetedges.
edge_flow.notes: Empty group or "*" is a silent no-op that leaves the P hash unchanged. No native equivalent.

relax.target: group is a point group; empty means all points.
relax.notes: modeler::relax has stepsize defaulting to 0, which makes it a silent no-op. Its working parms are group "*", grouptype "point", iterations 10, stepsize 1.0.

quad_flow.target: group is a PRIMITIVE group of exactly three faces meeting at one corner.
quad_flow.notes: Any other face selection is a silent no-op. No native equivalent.

mirror.target: group is a primitive group; empty means the whole input. Plane is origin plus dir.
mirror.notes: For duplicate-and-mirror the two nodes match. To make an existing centred mesh symmetric use modeler::symmetrize instead.

symmetrize.target: group is a primitive group; the plane comes from origin plus dir. Default value is "!_3d_hidden_primitives".
symmetrize.notes: clip=0 keeps the +dir half, mirrors it and welds the seam. clip=1 outputs only the clipped half.

mirror_group.target: group is the source selection; grouptype tokens "0" points, "1" edges, "2" primitives. sym_dirx/y/z default to all zero, always set the plane.
mirror_group.notes: Geometry is untouched, only a group is written, and only for source components on the +dir side. Writes no group at all when nothing matches, so always re-read.

crease_subd_preview.target: group is an edge group; inline "p<a>-<b>" list or an upstream edge group name.
crease_subd_preview.notes: Writes the same creaseweight vertex attribute as the native crease SOP; downstream subdivide gives an identical P hash.

preview_subd.target: No group; operates on the whole input.
preview_subd.notes: Emits real geometry, byte-identical to subdivide osdcc at the same iteration count.

subdivide_level1.target: The primitive group parm is named subdivide, not group; creases is a separate edge group field.
output_groups: creases (only when outputcrease is set to 1)
subdivide_level1.notes: algorithm tokens houdini|mantra|osdcc|osdloop|osdbilinear. Use osdbilinear for linear splitting that keeps the silhouette.

clean_edges.target: group is an edge group; "*" or empty both mean every edge.
clean_edges.notes: Dissolves coplanar edges in one node. The native route needs groupcreate plus dissolve and the groupbase trap below.

dissolve.target: group is an edge group name or an inline "p<a>-<b>" list.
dissolve.notes: Deterministic. Pair with groupcreate for angle-based selection and remember to set groupbase to 0 there.

group_sharp_edges.target: Scans the whole input unless group restricts it; writes an edge group.
group_sharp_edges.notes: outputgroup defaults to 0, which cooks fine but writes no group at all. Set it to 1.

polydoctor_check.target: group is a primitive group; empty means the whole input.
polydoctor_check.notes: Every detection parm is an ignore|mark|repair menu; mark reports without editing geometry. creategrps=1 is what writes those four groups (the node appends _grp to the parm values).
